description:
FILED s470bi (Opus, 2026-09-05) while fixing #1083 (the task named this probe).
PRE-EXISTING, SILENT.

`s///ee` evaluates the replacement, then evaluates THE RESULT as perl code.
PCL emits a single `:e` and stops after the first evaluation, so the result is
the replacement's VALUE where perl runs it as a program.

REPRO (scratch/s470bi/p1083/ee.pl):

    my $s = "3";  (my $t = $s) =~ s/(\d)/'$1+1'/ee;  print "ee: $t\n";
    my $u = "3";  $u =~ s/(\d)/'$1+1'/e;             print "e:  $u\n";
    my $v = "ab"; my $code = '"X" . uc($1)';
    $v =~ s/(a)/$code/ee;                            print "ee2: $v\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  ee: 4        e: $1+1     ee2: XAb
  PCL:          ee: $1+1     e: $1+1     ee2: "X" . uc($1)b

So `/ee` currently behaves EXACTLY like `/e` -- the second `e` is dropped on
the floor, and the substitution puts the unevaluated source text into the
string.  Nothing is printed either way.

WHERE: the modifier loop that builds a substitution's flags counts each letter
once (PPI's own `get_modifiers` does the same -- it returns `e => 1` for `ee`,
which #1083's classifier works around by counting the trailing modifier
letters of the token text).  The emitter needs the same count, and then an
extra `p-eval` of the first evaluation's RESULT, with the capture alist and
$1..$N live -- perl re-enters the compiler per match.

RELATED: #1083 (shipped s470bi) already treats `s///ee` as a runtime-compile
event for CV cloning, and its guard row asserts the CLONE, not the value --
so that row keeps passing when this is fixed.

perl-tests / companion rows behind it: not surveyed (grep for `ee` modifiers
in perl-tests/subst.t and t/op/subst.t before starting).

=== DONE (s470br) ===
SHIPPED.  Each `e` is one round.  The COUNT comes from the token's trailing
modifier letters -- `Pl::Parser2::_regex_modifier_text`, #1083's existing
reading, reached through a runtime `require` because a compile-time `use` of
Parser2 from ExprToCL is circular (the #435 pattern; ONE reading, not a copy) --
and each extra round wraps the lambda body in `_gen_eval_string_form`, the SAME
emission a written-out `eval STRING` gets, so it carries the capture alist and
the site's features rather than a bare (p-eval â¦) that could not see a lexical.

BARS: corpus-diff 3 of 111 -- closure.t and eval.t (the only two corpus files
with an `s///ee`, surveyed before running) plus magic.t from #1115; silent drops
5 unchanged.  emission-ab over the 74 files carrying either shape: 67 DIFF / 13
SAME / RCDIFF 0, every DIFF explained.  Companion re/subst.t 205/67 = its
snapshot row, ROW DIFF 0/0/0/0.  Generation v2-791.  Five guard rows in
Pl/t/transpile-test-08.t through test_transpile, so REAL PERL is the oracle for
each; the `/e` row is the inverse guard against widening onto single-`e`, and on
a base extraction the four `/ee` rows fail while that one passes.  File wall
time 3 s.
subject: s///ee behaves as s///e: the SECOND e must evaluate the first evaluation's RESULT as perl code (s/(\d)/'$1+1'/ee gives $1+1 where perl gives 4)
